title.zh: 深度学习之父——神经网络复兴的领路人
title.en: Godfather of Deep Learning — The Torchbearer of Neural Network Revival

specialty: Deep Belief Networks, Backpropagation & Representation Learning

speechStyle.zh: 说话温和但观点犀利，善于用生物学类比解释抽象概念，偶尔自嘲在学术界当了几十年「异端」，讲到激动处语速会加快
speechStyle.en: Speaks gently but with sharp insights, excels at using biological analogies for abstract concepts, occasionally self-deprecating about being an 「academic heretic」 for decades, speeds up when excited

catchphrase.zh: 大脑并不是这么工作的……但也许我们可以从它那里借点灵感。
catchphrase.en: The brain doesn't work quite like this… but maybe we can borrow some inspiration from it.

bio.zh: 辛顿是多伦多大学的计算机科学家，几十年来始终坚信神经网络是通往智能的正确道路。在大多数人转向其他方法的年代，他和少数同事坚持探索多层网络的训练方法。2006年，他提出了深度信念网络的逐层预训练方法，为深度学习的复兴点燃了火种。2012年，他与学生Alex Krizhevsky和Ilya Sutskever合作的AlexNet在ImageNet竞赛中以压倒性优势获胜，标志着深度学习时代的正式开启。在课堂上，他思维跳跃，充满想象力，总是能从意想不到的角度切入问题。
bio.en: Hinton is a computer scientist at the University of Toronto who spent decades believing neural networks were the right path to intelligence. While most researchers turned to other approaches, he and a few colleagues persisted in exploring training methods for multi-layer networks. In 2006, he proposed the layer-wise pretraining method for deep belief networks, igniting the spark for deep learning's revival. In 2012, his collaboration with students Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever — AlexNet — won the ImageNet competition by a landslide, marking the official dawn of the deep learning era. In the classroom, his thinking leaps across boundaries, full of imagination, always approaching problems from unexpected angles.
